00335.title: Imatinib for GIST
00335.context: KIT-positive GIST: unresectable/metastatic treatment or adjuvant treatment after resection
00335.purpose: For unresectable or metastatic GIST, imatinib aims to control disease and symptoms. After removal of higher-risk GIST, adjuvant treatment aims to reduce the chance of recurrence. These are different treatment goals and must be clearly recorded.
00335.label: Imatinib every day; no routine break

agents.name: Imatinib
agents.type: Oral targeted therapy: tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.explanation: Imatinib blocks certain kinase proteins, including KIT and PDGFRA, that can drive susceptible GIST cells. The exact tumour mutation affects sensitivity; a KIT-positive label alone does not replace specialist molecular review. Normal tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report rapid weight gain, swelling, new breathlessness, fever, unusual bleeding, severe rash or yellow eyes promptly. Keep blood tests even if you feel well.
risks: Nausea, diarrhoea, abdominal discomfort, fatigue, muscle cramps and rash
Swelling around the eyes or elsewhere; occasionally severe fluid retention or heart failure
Low blood counts with infection, anaemia or bleeding
Liver injury, occasionally severe; kidney function may decline with treatment
Rare severe skin reactions, gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation, hepatitis B reactivation and small-vessel clotting that can injure blood cells and kidneys
Fertility or pregnancy harm; discuss product-specific contraception and breastfeeding

anatomy: Tiredness, muscle cramps or weakness can affect daily activity. Report new or severe symptoms; do not assume all weakness is ordinary fatigue.
Nausea or mouth symptoms can affect eating and drinking. Ask for practical symptom support early.
Rapid weight gain, new swelling or breathlessness may indicate fluid retention and needs prompt assessment.
Regular blood tests detect liver effects. Report yellow eyes, dark urine or significant abdominal pain urgently.
Kidney function is monitored during treatment. Report reduced urine, marked swelling or difficulty drinking.
Low counts can cause infection, anaemia or bleeding. Fever, chills or sudden illness requires immediate oncology contact.
Report persistent diarrhoea. Severe abdominal pain, black stools or other significant bleeding needs urgent assessment.
Rash can occur. Widespread blistering, peeling skin or mouth/eye involvement needs urgent help.
00335.schedule: The usual NCCP starting dose is 400 mg by mouth every day with food. For progression in advanced disease, a specialist may consider 800 mg daily as 400 mg twice daily. Adjuvant treatment after resection is described as up to 3 years in this NCCP document; your specialist confirms duration using current risk and evidence. The 28-day graphic is a reference view, not a treatment break or fixed course.
00335.administration: Take the prescribed dose with a meal and a large glass of water. Take doses consistently. If swallowing is difficult, ask the pharmacy about the exact supplied product before changing how it is taken.
00335.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, ECG and hepatitis B screening. Confirm GIST pathology, mutation information, treatment intent, prior medicines, fluid status and pregnancy/fertility plans.
00335.monitoring: Full blood count every 2 weeks for the first 12 weeks, then monthly. Kidney and liver tests monthly. Review weight, swelling, breathlessness, rash, bowel symptoms and interactions; additional tests depend on findings. Imaging follows the individual disease or recurrence-monitoring plan.
00335.support: A routine tablet break, growth factor or steroid course is not part of this schedule. Nausea prevention depends partly on dose: the NCCP oral emetogenic category changes above 400 mg/day. Use the individually prescribed symptom plan and report persistent diarrhoea, vomiting or swelling. Hepatitis B follow-up is individualised if screening is positive.
00335.prep: Confirm whether treatment is for advanced disease or after surgery, and the exact daily dose. Review all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal products; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Never increase the dose after a scan or a missed dose without the team.
00335.access: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.
00335.wider: GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/PDGFRA and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.
00335.scope: This is NCCP 00335 for GIST, not an imatinib schedule for leukaemia or another tumour. Advanced and adjuvant aims/durations differ. Low-risk adjuvant GIST is outside this source indication; molecular resistance can also alter suitability.
00335.trial: SSGXVIII/AIO: three versus one year of adjuvant imatinib
00335.evidence: An early study in advanced GIST demonstrated tumour responses and disease control with imatinib; it was not an adjuvant study. Separately, in high-risk GIST after surgery, three years of adjuvant imatinib improved recurrence-free and overall survival compared with one year at long follow-up. Keep these treatment settings distinct.
00335.caveat: The NCCP document describes up to three years after surgery. Later IMADGIST evidence supports disease-free survival benefit from extending treatment in selected high-risk patients, so three years should not be labelled universally optimal or imposed as an automatic stop. Advanced GIST requires its own evidence and continuation discussion.
doses: Take the prescribed dose every day with food; this reference graphic does not create a break.
00335.course: Continuous treatment; intent and duration individually confirmed
00335.missed: If you miss an imatinib dose, take it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; then skip it and return to the usual schedule. Never double a dose. Ask the team what to do after vomiting; do not take a replacement dose without advice.
00335.urgent: Rapid weight gain, new swelling, breathlessness, severe rash, jaundice, fever or significant bleeding needs prompt assessment.

00325.title: Sunitinib for GIST: 28 days on, 14 days off
00325.context: Unresectable or metastatic GIST after imatinib resistance or intolerance
00325.purpose: Sunitinib aims to slow GIST growth and help symptoms after imatinib has stopped working or cannot be tolerated. The team reviews previous treatment, tumour biology, your health and priorities before choosing the schedule.
00325.label: Sunitinib days 1–28; break days 29–42

agents.name: Sunitinib
agents.type: Oral targeted therapy: tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.explanation: Sunitinib blocks several kinases, including KIT and blood-vessel growth receptors. After imatinib resistance or intolerance it may slow GIST growth. Its effects on normal blood vessels and other tissues explain the need for blood-pressure, heart, thyroid and organ-function monitoring.
agents.watch: Report painful hands or feet, worsening diarrhoea, bleeding, chest pain, breathlessness, faintness, severe headache or a blistering rash promptly. Do not restart after a serious reaction without oncology review.
risks: Fatigue, appetite or taste change, nausea, diarrhoea and mouth soreness
Painful hand-foot skin reaction, skin or hair colour changes and rash
High blood pressure, thyroid dysfunction and low blood counts
Serious liver injury, heart weakness or rhythm problems, bleeding or blood clots
Rare bowel perforation, pancreatic inflammation, severe skin reactions, neurological syndromes or kidney injury/protein loss, including small-vessel clotting
Impaired wound healing and jaw-bone injury (osteonecrosis); fertility/pregnancy harm
Rare severe infection, low blood glucose or brain effects causing unexplained confusion, seizures or visual change

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or new visual problems can signal serious blood-pressure or brain effects. Seek urgent help.
Soreness and taste change can reduce intake. Use gentle mouth care and ask for symptom support early.
Attend blood-pressure checks. Chest pain, new breathlessness, fainting or severe palpitations needs urgent assessment.
Liver injury can occur without early symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report yellow eyes or dark urine.
Report reduced urine, swelling or dehydration. Your team checks kidney function and may check urine protein when indicated.
Report fever, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding. Heavy bleeding, black stools or coughing blood needs urgent help.
Ask early about diarrhoea. Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or inability to drink requires urgent advice.
Report soreness, redness, cracks or blisters early. Reduce rubbing and heat and follow the skin-care plan.
00325.schedule: NCCP 00325: sunitinib 50 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–28, followed by 14 days without sunitinib. Repeat the 42-day cycle only as confirmed by your team. Dose reductions or additional holds may be needed; symptoms and monitoring continue during the planned break.
00325.administration: Swallow the prescribed capsules with water, with or without food. Take at a consistent time each treatment day. Use the written calendar to distinguish treatment days from the planned break.
00325.baseline: Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, thyroid function and blood pressure. Review cardiac history, interacting medicines, electrolytes and whether ECG/ECHO/MUGA are needed. The source requires baseline cardiac evaluation and further investigations according to risk and symptoms.
00325.monitoring: Blood count and kidney/liver tests before each cycle, thyroid tests every 12 weeks and blood pressure at each attendance. Cardiac assessment and further tests depend on risk, symptoms and previous abnormalities.
00325.support: No routine separate premedication is specified. This oral schedule has minimal-to-low emetogenic potential; symptom medicines are prescribed individually. Ask for a hand-foot skin-care plan and early diarrhoea support. Treat blood-pressure or thyroid problems as prescribed. Tell the team before surgery, dental procedures or starting any new medicine.
00325.prep: Confirm the exact calendar and dose strength before each cycle. Review all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, especially CYP3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Keep a blood-pressure and symptom record if your team asks.
00325.access: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.
00325.wider: GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/PDGFRA and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.
00325.scope: This is the 42-day GIST context of NCCP 00325. The 21-day and 42-day schedules have different dosing calendars and some different source eligibility/organ-function rules; do not swap them yourself.
00325.trial: Randomised sunitinib trial after imatinib failure in GIST
00325.evidence: A placebo-controlled trial showed that sunitinib delayed GIST progression after imatinib resistance or intolerance. The studied schedule was 50 mg daily for four weeks followed by two weeks off.
00325.caveat: Trial findings apply to previously treated GIST and the studied schedule. They do not predict an individual response or establish benefit in renal cancer, another treatment line or the alternative 21-day calendar.
doses: Take the prescribed once-daily dose on treatment days.
No sunitinib during the planned break unless your team gives a revised prescription; monitoring and symptom reporting continue.
00325.course: Repeat while benefit and tolerability justify treatment
00325.missed: Skip a missed sunitinib dose and take the next scheduled dose at the usual time. Do not take an extra or double dose. Ask the team about vomiting or repeated missed doses.
00325.urgent: Chest pain, new breathlessness, fainting, severe headache, confusion, significant bleeding, severe abdominal pain or blistering skin requires urgent assessment.

00719.purpose: Sunitinib aims to slow GIST growth and help symptoms after imatinib has stopped working or cannot be tolerated. The team reviews previous treatment, tumour biology, your health and priorities before choosing the schedule.
00719.label: Sunitinib days 1–14; break days 15–21

00244.title: Regorafenib for GIST
00244.context: Unresectable or metastatic GIST after imatinib and sunitinib
00244.purpose: Regorafenib aims to control GIST after progression on, or intolerance to, both imatinib and sunitinib. Your team explains the likely benefit, uncertainty, alternatives and the monitoring needed for your circumstances.
00244.label: Regorafenib days 1–21; break days 22–28

agents.name: Regorafenib
agents.type: Oral targeted therapy: tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.mechanism: Blocks several growth and blood-vessel signals
agents.explanation: Regorafenib inhibits several kinases that help tumour cells grow and blood vessels support them. In GIST it is used after imatinib and sunitinib. Effects on healthy tissues make skin care, blood-pressure checks and early liver monitoring particularly important.
agents.watch: Report sore hands or feet early. Seek urgent help for yellow eyes, dark urine, severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache or confusion.
risks: Hand-foot skin reaction, rash, mouth soreness, fatigue and reduced appetite
Diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, dehydration and weight loss
High blood pressure and changes in thyroid function
Liver injury, sometimes severe or fatal; frequent early blood tests are essential
Infection, anaemia, low platelets and bleeding; rare heart ischaemia, bowel perforation or abnormal bowel connections (fistulas)
Impaired wound healing and pregnancy harm
Rare severe skin reactions, artery-wall bulging or tearing, small-vessel clotting with kidney injury, or brain effects causing confusion, seizures or visual changes

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or new visual problems can signal serious blood-pressure or brain effects. Seek urgent help.
Soreness and taste change can reduce intake. Use gentle mouth care and ask for symptom support early.
Attend blood-pressure checks. Chest pain, new breathlessness, fainting or severe palpitations needs urgent assessment.
Liver injury can occur without early symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report yellow eyes or dark urine.
Report reduced urine, swelling or dehydration. Your team checks kidney function and may check urine protein when indicated.
Report fever, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding. Heavy bleeding, black stools or coughing blood needs urgent help.
Ask early about diarrhoea. Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or inability to drink requires urgent advice.
Report soreness, redness, cracks or blisters early. Reduce rubbing and heat and follow the skin-care plan.
00244.schedule: NCCP 00244 uses regorafenib 160 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle, followed by 7 days off. The team may reduce the dose in 40 mg steps or interrupt treatment; do not change the dose or restart independently.
00244.administration: Swallow tablets whole with water after a light, low-fat meal, at a consistent time. Your pharmacy supplies the written food and dose instructions for the product you receive.
00244.baseline: Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, thyroid function and blood pressure. Review interacting medicines, skin and foot problems, recent/planned surgery and cardiac/QT risk. Lipase/amylase and ECG are checked when indicated.
00244.monitoring: Liver tests at least every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, then monthly or more often as indicated. Blood pressure weekly for the first 6 weeks, then before each cycle and as needed. Blood count/kidney tests regularly; thyroid/pancreatic tests and cardiac review when indicated. Monitor INR closely with warfarin.
00244.support: No routine separate premedication is specified; oral emetogenic potential is minimal-to-low. Start the agreed hand-foot skin-care measures and report painful areas early. Use prescribed diarrhoea, nausea, blood-pressure or thyroid treatment. Tell the team before surgery or dental procedures because healing may be affected.
00244.prep: Confirm that both prior imatinib and sunitinib treatments have been reviewed. Reconcile all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, including warfarin and CYP3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Agree liver-test and blood-pressure appointments before starting.
00244.access: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.
00244.wider: GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/PDGFRA and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.
00244.scope: This treatment plan is for GIST after both imatinib and sunitinib. Prior serious reactions remain relevant even when a current test or symptom has improved; an explicit oncology restart decision is required after a safety hold.
00244.trial: GRID: regorafenib after imatinib and sunitinib in advanced GIST
00244.evidence: GRID compared regorafenib plus best supportive care with placebo plus best supportive care in advanced GIST after imatinib and sunitinib. Regorafenib improved progression-free survival. This explains its later-line disease-control role.
00244.caveat: Progression-free survival is not the same as a proven overall-survival gain or an individual prognosis. Crossover complicates overall-survival interpretation. Do not use colorectal CORRECT or liver-cancer RESORCE results as GIST estimates.
doses: Take the prescribed dose after a light, low-fat meal.
Do not take regorafenib during the scheduled break unless your team has revised the plan; checks and symptom reporting continue.
00244.course: Repeat while benefit and tolerability justify treatment
00244.missed: Take a missed dose when remembered on the same day. Do not take two doses on one day. Do not take extra tablets after vomiting; contact the team if vomiting continues.
00244.urgent: Severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, confusion, yellow eyes or dark urine requires urgent assessment.
